responses.content:
World War II ended on two separate occasions: one in Europe and one in the Pacific.

In Europe, World War II officially came to an end with the formal surrender of Germany, known as V-E Day (Victory in Europe Day), which occurred on May 8, 1945. This date is widely recognized as the end of the war in Europe.

However, the actual fighting and occupation in Eastern Europe continued until the Soviet Union declared victory over Germany on April 9, 1945, with the capture of Berlin. The formal surrender took place on May 2, 1945, when German Field Marshal Wilhelm Keitel signed the unconditional surrender document at the Supreme Headquarters Allied Expeditionary Force (SHAEF) in Reims, France.

In the Pacific, Japan's formal surrender took place on September 2, 1945, aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, Japan. This date marks the official end of World War II in the Pacific Theater. The atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki on August 6 and 9, 1945, respectively, had already weakened Japan's ability to continue fighting, leading to the Japanese government's decision to surrender unconditionally.

Note: These dates are widely recognized by historians and are supported by verifiable evidence from official documents, photographs, and eyewitness accounts.
